name: ANSI/IEEE differential voltmeter symbol
summary: IEEE-library differential voltmeter form reading the difference between two voltages, for example across a synchronising point.
description: A differential voltmeter reads the difference between two applied voltages rather than either voltage alone. In synchronising panels it is wired between the incoming and running VT secondaries so the operator can see when the voltage difference is small enough to close the breaker.

The symbol does not show whether both inputs come from the same phase, or whether VT ratios are matched. If the two VTs have different ratios or phase shifts through a transformer, the reading is meaningless unless interposing correction is drawn.
readingNotes: Confirm both inputs are taken from the same phase pair.
Check the VT ratios on both sides of the closing point.
drawingChecklist: Note any ratio or angle correction
distinction: A differential voltmeter shows the difference between two voltages; a double voltmeter shows both voltages on separate scales.
